name: AGV

driveSpeed.label: Drive speed (m/s)
driveSpeed.desc: How fast the truck travels between waypoints.

turnSpeed.label: Turn speed (°/s)
turnSpeed.desc: How fast it pivots on the spot. Every move turns to face the target, drives, then turns to the waypoint heading, so this sets much of the cycle time on short hops.

liftSpeed.label: Fork lift speed (m/s)
liftSpeed.desc: How fast the tines raise and lower to the height the waypoint asks for.

maxLiftHeight.label: Max fork height (m)
maxLiftHeight.desc: Ceiling on the tines, whatever a waypoint asks for. Set it to the top beam of the racking the truck actually serves.

reverseRange.label: Back-out range
reverseRange.desc: How close a target behind the truck, at about the heading it already holds, has to be for it to back out instead of turning round, the way tines withdraw from a rack bay. 0 means it always turns.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Connect this truck to a PLC program. Its tags appear once this is on. Without a program the truck parks at home.

commandTag.label: Command tag (0 = home, 1+ = waypoint)
commandTag.desc: Which row of the waypoint table to drive to, as an index: 0 is home, 1 the second row and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. An index past the end of the table is ignored, and the truck stays put rather than guessing.

executeTag.label: Execute tag (rising edge runs the move)
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start the move. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each move. An edge arriving mid-move is ignored.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true while idle)
doneTag.desc: True while the truck is parked and ready. It drops for every move it accepts, even one that finishes at once, and comes back once the move is over and Execute is released (or half a second has passed), so wait for it before pulsing Execute again.

forkTag.label: Fork tag (true grabs, false releases)
forkTag.desc: Clamp or release whatever is sitting on the tines. It is read continuously rather than on an edge, so hold it true for the whole carry and drop it only once the load is where it belongs.

waypoints.label: Waypoints (row 0 = home)
waypoints.desc: The stops this truck knows, one row each: X and Z in the scene, the heading, and the tine height. Row 0 is home and the command tag picks a row. The tines move while it drives, except on a back-out, where they reach height first.
